newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Friday:

In answer to a question, spokesman Gerry Kiely denied that the Commission had received the final report on public health risks of gelatine manufacturing methods from the Gelatine Manufacturers of Europe before taking its decision to consider the processing methods safe last April. He added that to suggest that anybody in the Commission or in the Scientific Committees had had information on the final report was rubbish and total fabrication.
Kiely also said that the ban on British gelatine would not be lifted, in any case, until positive results came out of current research.

Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida confirmed that Commission President Jacques Santer had regular contacts with NATO Secretary General Javier Solana but denied any formal mechanism on future enlargements.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/96/1028: Infringement procedure, Commission sends reasoned opinion to Belgium concerning directive on sulphur content of liquid fuels.
- IP/96/1029: Infringement procedure, Commission sends reasoned opinion to Belgium, Ireland, Luxembourg, Spain and Portugal on non-implementation of GMO directive.
- IP/96/1030: Visit of South Africa's Deputy Presisent Thabo Mbeki to the Commission (14 November 1996).
- IP/96/1032: Commission joins the search to find Europe's young driver of the year.
- Speech/96/289: Summary of speech by Commissioner Anita Gradin on the fights against organized crime in Europe.
- Speech/96/290: Speech by Commissioner Christos Papoutsis on Europe's 500 annual conference.
- Speech/96/291: Address by Commissioner Franz Fischler before the world food summit.
- Speech/96/292: Presentation by Commissioner Mario Monti at the money laundering conference.
- Speech/96/294: Speech by Commissioner Ritt Bjerregaard at the third conference of the parties to the convention on biological diversity.
- Memo/96/110: Agenda of the Commission for the week from November 18- November 22.
- Memo/96/111: Background paper on the South African Republic and the European Union.
